$comment: Advisories the npm audit gate accepts, by GHSA id, each with the reason it
is accepted and a date by which it must be re-argued. Read by
This file can only ever shrink the gate for the exact ids listed. Anything
else at high or critical still fails. An entry whose advisory has stopped
appearing fails too, so a stale exception cannot quietly outlive its cause,
and so does an entry past its reviewBy date.

allow.title: MapLibre GL JS: XSS Sanitizer Bypass in DOM.sanitize() via Live NamedNodeMap Removal Skip
allow.reachedVia: plotly.js bundles maplibre-gl for its map trace types
why: No fixed version exists to upgrade to: the advisory range is <=6.4.0,
which covers every maplibre-gl release, so this cannot be patched by
moving forward. npm's suggested 'fix' is a downgrade of plotly.js from
3.4.0 to 2.34.0, which does not patch anything; it removes maplibre-gl
because plotly 2.x bundled mapbox-gl instead, at the cost of a major
version regression across every chart in the app.
The vulnerable code is unreachable here. The advisory is an XSS bypass
in maplibre's DOM.sanitize(), which only runs once a map is
instantiated. uSTAT renders no map traces at all: there is no
scattermapbox, choroplethmapbox, scattermap, densitymap or choroplethmap
anywhere in frontend/src, so maplibre is bundled but never constructed.
Revisit when plotly.js ships a maplibre-gl above the advisory range, or
if a map trace is ever added to the app, whichever comes first.
